nodes.name: Ce-modified MCM-41 synthesis
nodes.procedure: Cerium modified mesostructured MCM-41 materials (Ce-MCM-41-50 containing 2.9 wt% CeO2 and Ce-MCM-41-10 containing 13.2 wt% CeO2) synthesis and structural characterization reported by O.A. González Vargas et al. [12]. Higher CeO2 loading partially collapses the MCM-41 pore system leading to less ordered mesostructure [13].
nodes.source_text: Cerium modified mesostructured MCM-41 materials´ synthesis and structural characterization is reported elsewhere [12]... upon incrementing the cerium load, the higher concentration of CeO2 partially collapses the pore system, leading to a less ordered MCM-41 mesostructure (Fig. 1B) [13].

nodes.characterization_summary: Ce M4,5-edge EELS shows white-line peaks at 883 eV (M5) and 901 eV (M4) with branching ratios >0.5 (Ce3+) dominant in Ce-MCM-41-50 (2.9 wt% CeO2) small nanoparticles and <0.5 (Ce4+) dominant in Ce-MCM-41-10 (13.2 wt% CeO2) larger nanoparticles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Subregions of 25-integrated EEL spectra extracted from SI in Fig. 3A shows spectra with ionization edge M4,5 branching ratio, where M5 peak higher intensity is an indication of oxygen deficient Ce2O3 (Ce3+)... in sample with a small amount of CeO2 most M5 peaks had larger integral intensity than M4 peaks corresponding to values of M4,5 branching ratio larger than 0.5.

properties.description: Cerium M4,5 absorption edge in X-ray absorption spectroscopy

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM imaging reveals Ce atoms distribution: well-preserved ordered MCM-41 mesostructure with scattered Ce at 2.9 wt% CeO2 (Ce-MCM-41-50); partial pore collapse and less ordered structure at 13.2 wt% CeO2 (Ce-MCM-41-10).
nodes.evidence_snippet: On the HAADF micrographs higher contrast of heavier cerium atoms shows how it is scattered on the MCM-41 mesostructure in the sample with low cerium concentration (Fig. 1A), the well preserved ordered structure can be observed... However, upon incrementing the cerium load, the higher concentration of CeO2 partially collapses the pore system, leading to a less ordered MCM-41 mesostructure (Fig. 1B).
